rv.q: If a rare tragicomedy by Ivan Turgenev isn't your idea of a great night out, who can blame you? After the sad fiasco of the Old Even with Iain Glen - an excellent actor but not quite a star, Vic's geriatric Much Ado About Nothing, it is a relief, as well as a his success in Game of Thrones pleasure, to report that this new notwithstanding...
Bailey's production, which is horribly funny and deeply touching, marks an impressive return to form by the Old Vic.
This is in no small part due to a pair of magnificent central performances.
Lucy Bailey's production is watchable enough, but what the play lacks is the nuanced layering of Chekhov and his adroit management of the narratives of multiple characters.

Iain Glen brings admirable grace to Kuzovkin, a shattered man grasping at his dignity, and Richard McCabe's monstrous, peacocking Tropatchov is like a malignant force of nature, devouring your attention.
